overview: More than 35 White Sea fossils document a bilateral benthic animal with a foot-like region and non-mineralized dorsal cover; molluscan affinity remains bounded.

ecology.diet: Surface feeding inferred; no radula is preserved
ecology.locomotion: Benthic crawling inferred from the foot-like region
ecology.guild: Mobile benthic feeder inferred from body form and associated traces

evidenceSummary: The sample supports body-plan reconstruction, but does not preserve a radula or establish crown-Mollusca membership, direct ancestry or a complete geographic range.

commonNameZh: 布尔吉斯页岩齿谜虫样本
overview: A 189-specimen sample repeatedly preserves transverse tooth rows, a broad foot and mantle-groove structures; radular homology remains an interpretation.

ecology.diet: Benthic feeding inferred from tooth rows and body plan
ecology.locomotion: Crawling inferred from the broad foot
ecology.guild: Mobile benthic feeder inferred from anatomy

evidenceSummary: Repeated preservation supports the feeding apparatus, foot and mantle-groove observations; molluscan radula homology and phylogenetic placement remain interpretations.

overview: Ninety newly prepared specimens reveal eyes, two tentacles, lateral fins and a funnel-like structure; a cephalopod interpretation remains contested.

ecology.diet: Predation inferred from eyes and tentacles
ecology.habitat: Marine water column inferred from fins and funnel-like structure
ecology.locomotion: Swimming inferred from lateral fins and funnel-like anatomy
ecology.guild: Nektonic predator is a functional interpretation

evidenceSummary: Soft anatomy is repeatedly preserved, but no diagnostic shell, siphuncle, beak or radula is known; cephalopod affinity therefore remains contested.

commonNameZh: 晚阿特达班期小米克里纳虫骨片组合样本
overview: Micrina material from four localities in three broadly synchronous late Atdabanian carbonate units was reconstructed as a sessile bivalved organism. Sellate sclerites preserve paired muscle scars, whereas mitral apophyses are interpreted as muscle platforms; valve homology and stem-brachiopod placement remain comparative hypotheses rather than preserved articulation.

ecology.diet: Not directly preserved; feeding mode is unresolved
ecology.habitat: Sessile marine carbonate setting inferred from the reconstructed attachment
ecology.locomotion: Sessile interpretation; locomotion is not observed
ecology.bodySize: Millimetre-scale phosphatic sclerites; whole-body size is not directly established
ecology.guild: Sessile benthic ecology is inferred from reconstruction, not directly observed

traits: Mitral phosphatic sclerites with apophyses interpreted as muscle platforms
Sellate phosphatic sclerites with paired muscle scars
evidenceSummary: Sellate muscle scars, mitral apophyses and the late Atdabanian material are documented directly, but the muscle-platform interpretation, assembled whole body, valve homology and stem-brachiopod placement are tested interpretations. This profile records a bounded study sample, not a global genus duration or direct ancestry.

commonNameZh: 澄江管状触手冠动物样本
overview: The referred 710-specimen Yuganotheca sample from the Yu’anshan Member collectively supports a reconstruction combining paired agglutinated valves, a lophophore, tube and pedicle; individual fossils do not all preserve this entire suite. The character mosaic supports comparison near the brachiopod–phoronid stem region but does not resolve exact homology or ancestry.

ecology.diet: Suspension feeding inferred from the preserved lophophore
ecology.locomotion: Attached interpretation inferred from the pedicle; movement is not observed
ecology.guild: Suspension-feeding interpretation is limited to the reconstructed specimen anatomy

traits: Paired agglutinated valves around a lophophoral chamber
Bipartite tube with a median collar
Long pedicle with an inferred coelomic space
evidenceSummary: The referred Chengjiang sample supplies the anatomical mosaic and formal stratigraphic context collectively; no individual fossil is asserted to preserve every reconstructed feature. Exact homology of the valves and tube, as well as the brachiopod–phoronid stem position, remain topology-dependent; the profile is not a global species range or direct-ancestor claim.
